evidence_gaps_add: No printed table compares several reanalysis methods by new confirmed diagnoses on the same unsolved cohort. Kaschta et al. 2026 (medRxiv 10.64898/2026.05.16.26352295) compares manual and automated (Talos) reanalysis of the same 219 unsolved genomes, but prints its per-method results only in prose; its Table 1 is an image and its supplement is per-patient clinical data. Nothing was imported from it.

Kaschta et al. 2026 also gave the automated arm the archived variant calls while the manual arm re-called variants with an updated DRAGEN version, so the two arms did not receive equal updated inputs.
The Solve-RD CNV reanalysis (Demidov et al. 2024) tables give review workload per caller; per-caller detection of the confirmed pathogenic CNVs appears only in the text.
The Exomiser reanalysis thresholds (Vestito et al. 2024) and the Talos evaluation cohorts are scored on diagnoses already known, which the use case's first exclusion keeps out of new-yield evidence.
AMELIE 3 (medRxiv 2020.12.29.20248974) reports alerts per patient per year, but its tables are images; not extracted.
Genet Med 2022 (Moon versus Exomiser on 80 nondiagnostic exomes) and J Mol Diagn 2019 (automated exome reanalysis) were not open access and were not retrieved.
use_case_changes.pinned_fields_note: No change is proposed to question, decision, inputs, output, setting or exclusions. These are pinned by the existing Talos programme judgement (use-case-mapping-20260930-342-3c7f6c5e1873).

summary_proposal.text: No source in this pass compares reanalysis methods by new confirmed diagnoses on the same unsolved cohort in a printed table. The printed comparisons measure review workload or recovery of diagnoses that were already known. In the Solve-RD reanalysis of 9171 unsolved exomes (Demidov et al. 2024), the three CNV callers returned very different numbers of calls for expert review: ExomeDepth 4205, ClinCNV 2782 and CoNIFER 862; ClinCNV was developed by a project partner. In 37 100,000 Genomes cases diagnosed after a new disease-gene association (Vestito et al. 2024, the Exomiser developers), the recommended flagging rule (phenotype score increase 0.2, variant score 0.8) caught 31 of the 37 diagnosed variants with 23 other variants flagged, while the loosest rule caught all 37 with 182 others flagged. On known diagnoses in the Talos evaluation cohorts, strict phenotype filtering cut the candidates returned in ACG trios from 487 to 403 and recovered 164 instead of 177 diagnoses. None of these figures is new diagnostic yield, and none is clinical validation.

number_trace.487 to 403, 177 to 164: uc-clinical-20260930-talos-acg-trio-{default,strict}-evaluation results 'count candidate variants flagged' and 'true-positive-count known diagnoses'

gaps: Same-cohort comparison of reanalysis methods by new confirmed diagnoses and measured review time: found only in prose (Kaschta et al. 2026).
Equal updated inputs: no source gives both arms the same updated calls, phenotypes and knowledge.
False alerts and retracted diagnoses per method across repeated cycles: not found in printed tables.

LIRICAL, AMELIE, Xrare, PhenIX, VarSeq and GEM reanalysis comparisons on unsolved cases: not found; their published comparisons are rankings of solved cases, which belong to the candidate-ranking use case.
Solve-RD Nature Medicine 2025 expert-review hours (Supplementary Table S3) describe one workflow, not a comparison; not extracted.
concerns_for_reviewer: Demidov et al. Methods give the ExomeDepth Bayes factor threshold as BF > 15 ('Alignment and definition of capture regions of interest' paragraph 2) and as discarding BF < 0.15 ('ExomeDepth workflow' paragraph 2). Both are kept in the configuration parameters; no evidence concern raised because no extracted value depends on the threshold printed.

Demidov et al. Supplementary Table 5's caption says 3,487 duplications and 4,362 deletions, while Supplementary Table 4 and the Results text give 3,487 deletions and 4,362 duplications. Supplementary Table 5 was not extracted; Table 4 matches the text.

Demidov et al. Supplementary Table 4 prints '.' as a thousands separator and ',' as the decimal separator. numeric_value converts them, and the extractor asserts that each caller's total equals Table 1; numeric_representation records this on each result.

Vestito et al. Supplementary Table 1 does not name the database releases compared. The 0.2/0.8 row (TP 31, FP 23) matches the text's February 2019 versus February 2022 result (54 candidates, 31 correct), so the table is read as that comparison; a claim records the inference.
Vestito et al. thresholds were tuned on the same 37 cases they are scored on.
ClinCNV evaluations are author_reported (developed by a Solve-RD partner, Methods); CoNIFER and ExomeDepth are independent_paper.
The seven Talos and Exomiser judgements reuse protocols already judged proxy for use-case-rare-disease-candidate-ranking. The same evaluations will therefore appear on both use-case pages.

Kaschta et al. 2026 is the most decision-relevant source found but was not extracted, because its per-method results are prose-only. A reviewer may want the standard to allow exact-locator prose transcription for this case. Its text also has internal inconsistencies (automated yield printed as 41.9% where 161 of 377 is 42.7%; the pipeline conversion share is 8.6% in the text and 9.6% in the Fig. 2 legend).
